\#\# 🤔 What is InSAR?

\*\*InSAR\*\* stands for \*\*Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar\*\*. It's a remote sensing technique that uses radar satellite images taken at different times to measure ground surface deformation (movement) with millimeter-to-centimeter precision. Think of it like comparing two photos of the same landscape taken months or years apart — except using radar waves instead of visible light.

\*\*Why it matters:\*\* InSAR helps scientists detect earthquakes, volcanic activity, landslides, land subsidence, and tectonic plate movements.

\#\# 1.3 Vim Survival Guide

\> 💡 \*\*What is Vim?\*\* Vim is a powerful terminal-based text editor found on virtually every Unix/Linux system. It has two main modes: \*\*Normal mode\*\* (for navigation and commands) and \*\*Insert mode\*\* (for typing text). This confuses beginners at first, but the basics are simple.

\#\#\# The Two Modes You Need to Know

\`\`\`

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                                  │

│   NORMAL MODE  ──── press i ────►  INSERT MODE   │

│   (commands)   ◄─── press Esc ───  (typing)      │

│                                                  │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

\`\`\`

\- When you first open Vim, you are in \*\*Normal mode\*\* — keypresses are interpreted as commands, not text.

\- Press \*\*\`i\`\*\* to enter \*\*Insert mode\*\* — now you can type text normally.

\- Press \*\*\`Esc\`\*\* to return to \*\*Normal mode\*\*.

\#\#\# Essential Vim Commands

\> ⚠️ All commands below are typed in \*\*Normal mode\*\* (press \`Esc\` first if you're unsure).

| Action | Keys | Description |

|--------|------|-------------|

| \*\*Open a file\*\* | \`vim filename\` | Run this in your terminal |

| \*\*Enter Insert mode\*\* | \`i\` | Start typing text at cursor position |

| \*\*Return to Normal mode\*\* | \`Esc\` | Stop typing, go back to command mode |

| \*\*Save the file\*\* | \`:w\` then \`Enter\` | \*\*W\*\*rite (save) the file |

| \*\*Quit Vim\*\* | \`:q\` then \`Enter\` | \*\*Q\*\*uit (only works if no unsaved changes) |

| \*\*Save and quit\*\* | \`:wq\` then \`Enter\` | \*\*W\*\*rite and \*\*q\*\*uit (this is the one you'll use most\!) |

| \*\*Quit without saving\*\* | \`:q\!\` then \`Enter\` | Force quit, discard all changes |

| \*\*Undo\*\* | \`u\` | Undo the last change |

| \*\*Redo\*\* | \`Ctrl \+ r\` | Redo (undo the undo) |

| \*\*Delete a line\*\* | \`dd\` | Deletes the entire line the cursor is on |

| \*\*Go to end of file\*\* | \`G\` (capital) | Jump to the last line |

| \*\*Go to beginning of file\*\* | \`gg\` | Jump to the first line |

| \*\*Search for text\*\* | \`/searchterm\` then \`Enter\` | Press \`n\` for next match, \`N\` for previous |

\#\#\# Vim Cheat Sheet — The Only Workflow You Need

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Open a file

vim myfile.txt

\# 2\. Press i to start typing

\# 3\. Type or edit your text

\# 4\. Press Esc when done typing

\# 5\. Type :wq and press Enter to save and exit

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*Stuck in Vim?\*\* Press \`Esc\` a few times, then type \`:q\!\` and press \`Enter\`. This will force-quit without saving. You can always start over.

\#\# 1.4 Create Your NASA EarthData \`.netrc\` File

\> 💡 \*\*What is \`.netrc\`?\*\* It's a hidden file that stores your login credentials so that scripts can automatically authenticate when downloading data from NASA servers. The \`.\` at the beginning means it's hidden — you won't see it with a normal \`ls\`, but \`ls \-la\` will show it.

\#\#\# Steps:

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Go to your home directory

cd \~

\# 2\. Open (or create) the .netrc file in Vim

vim .netrc

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Inside Vim, type exactly these 3 lines (replacing with YOUR credentials):

1\. Press \`i\` to enter Insert mode

2\. Type the following:

\`\`\`text

machine urs.earthdata.nasa.gov

login your\_earthdata\_login\_name

password your\_earthdata\_password

\`\`\`

3\. Press \`Esc\` to return to Normal mode

4\. Type \`:wq\` and press \`Enter\` to save and exit

\`\`\`bash

\# 3\. Secure the file so only you can read it

chmod 600 \~/.netrc

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify it worked:

\`\`\`bash

cat \~/.netrc

\# You should see your 3 lines displayed

\`\`\`

\> ⚠️ \*\*Security:\*\* Never share your \`.netrc\` file or commit it to Git. The \`chmod 600\` command ensures only you can read it.

\---

\#\# 1.5 Set Up Your \`\~/bin\` Directory

\> 💡 \*\*What is \`\~/bin\`?\*\* It's a personal folder for scripts and tools. When it's in your PATH (see below), you can run any script inside it from anywhere, just by typing its name.

\`\`\`bash

\# Create your personal bin directory (if it doesn't exist)

mkdir \-p \~/bin

\# Copy all LInOG processing scripts from the shared repository

cp /eggraid/sbin/\*.py \~/bin/

cp /eggraid/sbin/\*.sh \~/bin/

\# Make all scripts executable

chmod \+x \~/bin/\*

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

ls \~/bin/

\# You should see scripts like: find\_alos.sh, unzip\_ALOS-SLC.py,

\# unzip\_ALOS-SLC-pol.py, run\_unpack\_all\_cli.py, poststep04\_cleanup.py, etc.

\`\`\`

\---

\#\# 1.6 Configure Your PATH Variable

\> 💡 \*\*What is PATH?\*\* It's an environment variable that tells the system where to look for programs. By adding \`\~/bin\` to your PATH, you can type \`find\_alos.sh\` instead of \`/home/yourusername/bin/find\_alos.sh\`.

\`\`\`bash

\# Open your bash profile in Vim

vim \~/.bashrc

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Add these lines at the bottom:

1\. Press \`G\` to jump to the end of the file

2\. Press \`o\` to open a new line below and enter Insert mode

3\. Type:

\`\`\`bash

\# \=== LInOG InSAR Processing \===

export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"

\`\`\`

4\. Press \`Esc\`, then type \`:wq\` and press \`Enter\`

\#\#\# Reload so changes take effect:

\`\`\`bash

source \~/.bashrc

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

echo $PATH

\# You should see /home/yourusername/bin at the beginning

which find\_alos.sh

\# Should print: /home/yourusername/bin/find\_alos.sh

\`\`\`

\---

\#\# 1.7 Set Up Bash Aliases (Optional but Recommended)

\> 💡 \*\*What are aliases?\*\* Shortcuts for long commands you type frequently.

\`\`\`bash

vim \~/.bash\_aliases

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Add useful shortcuts:

1\. Press \`i\` to enter Insert mode

2\. Type:

\# Quick navigation

alias cdlinog='cd \~/projects/linog/insar'

alias cdwork='cd /eggraid/home/$USER/projects'

\# Quick process monitoring

\# Useful listing

\`\`\`

3\. Press \`Esc\`, then type \`:wq\` and press \`Enter\`

\#\#\# Reload:

\`\`\`bash

source \~/.bashrc

\`\`\`

\#\# 1.8 Monitor System Resources with \`htop\`

\> 💡 \*\*What is \`htop\`?\*\* A visual tool that shows you how much CPU and memory your processing jobs are using — like "Task Manager" on Windows.

\`\`\`bash

\# Launch htop

htop

\`\`\`

\*\*Key things to look for:\*\*

\- \*\*CPU bars\*\* at the top → shows how busy each processor core is

\- \*\*Mem bar\*\* → shows total memory usage

\- \*\*Your processes\*\* → listed below with CPU% and MEM% columns

\*\*Useful htop shortcuts:\*\*

| Key | Action |

|-----|--------|

| \`F5\` | Tree view (see parent/child processes) |

| \`u\` | Filter by user (type your username) |

| \`F9\` | Kill a stuck process |

| \`q\` | Quit htop |

\> ⚠️ \*\*Important:\*\* Always check \`htop\` before running heavy processing (like \`parallel\` jobs) to make sure the server isn't overloaded by other users.

\`\`\`bash

\# Create your project directory structure

mkdir \-p \~/projects/linog/insar/\[track\]/\[frame\]

cd \~/projects/linog/insar/\[track\]/\[frame\]

mkdir \-p \~/projects/linog/insar/448/0290

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

pwd

\# Should show: /eggraid/home/yourusername/projects/linog/insar/448/0290

\# (or /home/yourusername/projects/linog/insar/448/0290 depending on setup)

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*What are track and frame?\*\* Satellites follow fixed orbits called "tracks" (or paths). Each track is divided into "frames" — rectangular sections of the Earth's surface. Together, track \+ frame identify the specific area on the ground that the satellite imaged. For LInOG, we use ALOS track \*\*448\*\*, frame \*\*0290\*\*.

\# 3\. Pre-Stack Processing

This section covers turning raw ALOS satellite data into organized SLC (Single Look Complex) images ready for interferometric processing.

\---

\#\# 3.1 Overview

\`\`\`

Raw ALOS archive → Symlinked → Unzipped → Unpacked to SLC

\`\`\`

| Step | Script | Input | Output |

|------|--------|-------|--------|

| Find & link data | \`find\_alos.sh\` | Raw archive | Symlinks in \`raw/\` |

| Unzip data | \`unzip\_ALOS-SLC.py\` | Zipped files | Unzipped folders |

| Unpack to SLC | \`run\_unpack\_all\_cli.py\` | Unzipped folders | SLC directory |

\---

\#\# 3.2 Step 1: Find and Link Source Data

\> 💡 \*\*What is a symlink?\*\* A symbolic link (symlink) is like a shortcut. Instead of copying huge radar data files (which can be many gigabytes), we create "pointers" to where the original files live. This saves disk space.

\`\`\`bash

\# Make sure you're in your working directory

cd \~/projects/linog/insar/448/0290

\# Run the script to create symlinks to the source ALOS data

find\_alos.sh

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

ls \-la raw/

\# You should see symlinks (shown with \-\> arrows) pointing to /eggraid/data/alos/...

\`\`\`

\---

\#\# 3.3 Step 2: Unzip the Data

\> 💡 \*\*What's happening?\*\* The raw ALOS data comes in compressed (zipped) archives. This step extracts them.

\#\#\# Option A: Unzip ALL data (FBS \+ FBD)

\`\`\`bash

python \~/bin/unzip\_ALOS-SLC.py

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Option B: Unzip only a specific polarization mode

\> 💡 \*\*FBS vs FBD:\*\* ALOS PALSAR has two main modes:

\> \- \*\*FBS\*\* (Fine Beam Single) — single polarization, higher range resolution

\> \- \*\*FBD\*\* (Fine Beam Dual) — dual polarization, lower range resolution

\>

\> The mode affects pixel size and how we process the data later.

\`\`\`bash

\# Unzip only FBS data

python \~/bin/unzip\_ALOS-SLC-pol.py \--pol FBS

\# Unzip only FBD data

python \~/bin/unzip\_ALOS-SLC-pol.py \--pol FBD

\# See all available options

python \~/bin/unzip\_ALOS-SLC-pol.py \--help

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

ls unzipped/

\# You should see folders with ALOS scene IDs (dates)

\# Each folder should contain .LED, .IMG, and other files

\`\`\`

\---

\#\# 3.4 Step 3: Unpack All Data into SLC Directory

\> 💡 \*\*What is SLC?\*\* SLC stands for \*\*Single Look Complex\*\*. It's a processed radar image format where each pixel contains both amplitude (brightness) and phase (wave timing) information. The phase is what makes interferometry possible.

\`\`\`bash

\# This reads the unzipped data and creates properly formatted SLC files

run\_unpack\_all\_cli.py

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

ls SLC/

\# You should see directories named by date (e.g., 20070125, 20070612, 20090626\)

\# Each should contain .slc and .xml files

\# Count how many dates you have:

ls SLC/ | wc \-l

\# This tells you how many SAR acquisitions are available

\`\`\`

\> ⚠️ \*\*Troubleshooting:\*\* If \`run\_unpack\_all\_cli.py\` fails:

\> \- Check that \`unzipped/\` directory has data: \`ls unzipped/\`

\> \- Check for error messages — they usually indicate missing files or permission issues

\> \- Make sure ISCE2 is loaded in your environment: \`which stripmapApp.py\`

\---

\---

\# 4\. DEM Preparation

\> 💡 \*\*What is a DEM?\*\* A \*\*Digital Elevation Model\*\* is a 3D representation of the Earth's surface (a grid of elevation values). InSAR processing needs a DEM to:

\> 1\. Remove the topographic phase (the radar signal change caused by terrain, not ground movement)

\> 2\. Geocode results (place them on a map)

\---

\#\# 4.1 Option A: Copy the Pre-Made LInOG DEM (Recommended)

A stitched SRTM DEM already exists for the LInOG study area. This is the fastest option.

\`\`\`bash

\# Make sure you're in your frame working directory

cd \~/projects/linog/insar/448/0290

\# Copy the DEM directory

cp \-r /eggraid/data/dems/srtm/linog/DEM .

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

ls DEM/

\# You should see files like:

\# demLat\_N14\_N18\_Lon\_E120\_E123.dem.wgs84

\# demLat\_N14\_N18\_Lon\_E120\_E123.dem.wgs84.xml

\# demLat\_N14\_N18\_Lon\_E120\_E123.dem.wgs84.vrt

\`\`\`

\---

\#\# 4.2 Option B: Download Your Own SRTM DEM

\> Use this if you're processing a different area or need a custom DEM.

\> ⚠️ \*\*Prerequisite:\*\* You must have your \`.netrc\` file configured (see \[Section 1.4\](\#14-create-your-nasa-earthdata-netrc-file))

\`\`\`bash

\# Create and enter DEM directory

mkdir DEM

cd DEM

\# Download and stitch SRTM tiles

\# Replace coordinate bounds: \[min\_lat\] \[max\_lat\] \[min\_lon\] \[max\_lon\]

dem.py \-a stitch \-b \[min\_lat\] \[max\_lat\] \[min\_lon\] \[max\_lon\] \-r \-s 1 \-c \-u http://step.esa.int/auxdata/dem/SRTMGL1/

\`\`\`

\#\#\# For LInOG specifically:

\`\`\`bash

dem.py \-a stitch \-b 14 18 120 123 \-r \-s 1 \-c \-u http://step.esa.int/auxdata/dem/SRTMGL1/

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*What do these flags mean?\*\*

\>

\> | Flag | Meaning |

\> |------|---------|

\> | \`-a stitch\` | Action: download and stitch tiles together |

\> | \`-b 14 18 120 123\` | Bounding box: latitudes 14°N to 18°N, longitudes 120°E to 123°E |

\> | \`-r\` | Create a reference (WGS84) version |

\> | \`-s 1\` | 1 arc-second resolution (\~30 m) |

\> | \`-c\` | Correct for Earth's curvature |

\> | \`-u http://...\` | URL of the DEM data server |

\#\#\# Clean up temporary files:

\`\`\`bash

\# Remove individual tile files (we only need the stitched result)

rm demLat\*.dem demLat\*.dem.xml demLat\*.dem.vrt

\# Go back to your working directory

cd ..

\`\`\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

ls DEM/

\# Should have the stitched .dem.wgs84 file and its .xml and .vrt companions

\`\`\`

\# 5\. Stack Configuration & Baselines

This is where you tell ISCE2 how to pair your SAR images and set key processing parameters.

\---

\#\# 5.1 Key Concepts

\> 💡 \*\*Important terms for beginners:\*\*

\>

\> | Term | Meaning |

\> |------|---------|

\> | \*\*Stack\*\* | The collection of all your SAR images for one area |

\> | \*\*Reference (master) date\*\* | One image chosen as the "anchor" that all others are compared to |

\> | \*\*Baseline\*\* | The distance between satellite positions for two acquisitions |

\> | \*\*Perpendicular baseline\*\* | Component of baseline perpendicular to the radar look direction (affects InSAR quality) |

\> | \*\*Temporal baseline\*\* | Time gap between two acquisitions |

\> | \*\*Interferogram\*\* | The result of comparing two SAR images — encodes ground deformation |

\> | \*\*Multilooking\*\* | Averaging neighboring pixels to reduce noise (at the cost of resolution) |

\---

\#\# 5.2 Step 1: Generate the Baseline Plot

The baseline plot helps you visualize all your SAR acquisitions in time vs. perpendicular baseline space, so you can pick the best reference date.

\`\`\`bash

\# Make sure you're in your frame working directory

cd \~/projects/linog/insar/448/0290

\# Generate baseline plot (this does NOT process data yet — it plans the stack)

stackStripMap.py \-W interferogram \--nofocus \\

  \-s SLC \\

  \-d DEM/demLat\_N14\_N18\_Lon\_E120\_E123.dem.wgs84 \\

  \-t 730 \\

  \-b 1500 \\

  \-a 28 \\

  \-r 12 \\

  \-u snaphu

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*What do these parameters mean?\*\*

\>

\> | Parameter | Value | Meaning |

\> |-----------|-------|---------|

\> | \`-W interferogram\` | — | Workflow type: generate interferograms |

\> | \`--nofocus\` | — | Skip focusing (data is already SLC) |

\> | \`-s SLC\` | SLC | Path to the SLC directory |

\> | \`-d DEM/...\` | DEM file | Path to the DEM file |

\> | \`-t 730\` | 730 days | Maximum temporal baseline (time gap between pairs) |

\> | \`-b 1500\` | 1500 m | Maximum perpendicular baseline |

\> | \`-a 28\` | 28 | Number of looks in \*\*azimuth\*\* direction (along-track averaging) |

\> | \`-r 12\` | 12 | Number of looks in \*\*range\*\* direction (across-track averaging) |

\> | \`-u snaphu\` | snaphu | Phase unwrapping method |

\---

\#\# 5.3 Step 2: Review the Baseline Plot

The command above generates a file called \`pairs.pdf\`. You need to look at it to choose the best reference date.

\`\`\`bash

\# Copy the PDF to your local computer for viewing

\# Run this on YOUR LOCAL machine (not the server):

scp \[your\_username\]@felix:/eggraid/home/\[your\_username\]/projects/linog/insar/448/0290/pairs.pdf .

\# Example:

scp arieln@felix:/eggraid/home/arieln/projects/linog/insar/448/0290/pairs.pdf .

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*How to read the baseline plot:\*\*

\>

\> \`\`\`

\>       ↑ Perpendicular

\>       │ Baseline (m)

\>       │

\>       │        ●              ← Each dot \= one SAR acquisition

\>       │       / \\

\>       │      /   ●

\>       │  ●──/     \\──●

\>       │     \\     /

\>       │      ●───●

\>       │       \\

\>       │        ●

\>       ├────────────────────→  Time

\>       2007    2009    2011

\>

\>   IDEAL REFERENCE \= near the CENTER of both axes

\> \`\`\`

\>

\> \*\*The ideal reference date should be:\*\*

\> \- Near the \*\*middle\*\* of the time span

\> \- Near the \*\*middle\*\* of the perpendicular baseline range

\> \- This minimizes the maximum baseline to any other acquisition

\---

\#\# 5.4 Step 3: Re-run with Your Chosen Reference Date

After inspecting the baseline plot, set the reference date with the \`-m\` flag.

\`\`\`bash

\# For LInOG, the date 20090626 is near the center of the baseline plot

stackStripMap.py \-W interferogram \--nofocus \\

  \-s SLC \\

  \-d DEM/demLat\_N14\_N18\_Lon\_E120\_E123.dem.wgs84 \\

  \-t 730 \\

  \-b 1500 \\

  \-a 28 \\

  \-r 12 \\

  \-u snaphu \\

  \-m 20090626

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*Date format:\*\* Always use \`YYYYMMDD\` (year-month-day with no dashes). Example: June 26, 2009 → \`20090626\`

\#\#\# ✅ Verify:

\`\`\`bash

\# Check that run\_files were created

ls run\_files/

\# Should see: run\_01\_reference, run\_02\_focus\_split, run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp, etc.

\# Check the content of one run file

cat run\_files/run\_01\_reference

\# Should show ISCE2 processing commands

\`\`\`

\---

\---

\# 6\. ISCE2 Processing — Running the Pipeline

Now we run the actual InSAR processing. ISCE2 organizes this into numbered "run files" that must be executed \*\*in order\*\*.

\---

\#\# 6.1 Understanding Run Files

\> 💡 \*\*What are run files?\*\* Each \`run\_XX\_\*\` file is a shell script containing one or more commands. Some contain a single command (run sequentially with \`sh\`), while others contain many independent commands that can be run simultaneously using \`parallel\`.

| Run File | What It Does | Run Method | Est. Time |

|----------|-------------|------------|-----------|

| \`run\_01\_reference\` | Processes the reference (master) SLC image | \`sh\` (sequential) | \~10 min |

| \`run\_02\_focus\_split\` | Focuses and splits SLC data | \`sh\` (sequential) | \~10 min |

| \`run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp\` | Geocoding and coarse coregistration | \`parallel\` | \~30 min |

| \`run\_04\_refineSecondaryTiming\` | Refines alignment of secondary images | \`parallel\` | \~30 min |

| \*(cleanup step)\* | Removes intermediate files to save space | Python script | \~2 min |

| \`run\_05\_invertMisreg\` | Inverts misregistration estimates | \`sh\` (sequential) | \~5 min |

| \`run\_06\_fineResamp\` | Fine resampling of secondaries | \`parallel\` | \~20 min |

| \`run\_07\_grid\_baseline\` | Computes baseline grids | \`sh\` (sequential) | \~5 min |

| \`run\_08\_igram\` | Generates interferograms\! 🎉 | \`parallel\` | \~1–4 hours |

\---

\#\# 6.2 Running the Pipeline

\#\#\# Step 1: Reference Image Processing

\`\`\`bash

sh run\_files/run\_01\_reference

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*\`sh\`\*\* means "run this script in the shell, one command at a time."

\---

\#\#\# Step 2: Focus and Split

\`\`\`bash

sh run\_files/run\_02\_focus\_split

\`\`\`

\---

\#\#\# Step 3: Geocoding & Coarse Resampling (Parallel)

\`\`\`bash

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp

\`\`\`

\> 💡 \*\*What is \`parallel\`?\*\*

\> \`parallel\` is a tool that runs multiple commands simultaneously, using multiple CPU cores. This dramatically speeds up processing.

\>

\> | Part of Command | Meaning |

\> |----------------|---------|

\> | \`parallel\` | The GNU Parallel program |

\> | \`-j 4\` | Run \*\*4 jobs\*\* at the same time (adjust based on server load\!) |

\> | \`\< run\_files/...\` | Read commands from this file |

\>

\> ⚠️ \*\*Before using \`parallel\`:\*\* Check server load with \`htop\` first\! If other users are running heavy jobs, reduce \`-j 4\` to \`-j 2\` or even \`-j 1\` to be courteous.

\---

\#\#\# Step 4: Refine Secondary Timing (Parallel)

\`\`\`bash

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_04\_refineSecondaryTiming

\`\`\`

\---

\#\#\# Step 4.5: Cleanup (Important\!)

\`\`\`bash

poststep04\_cleanup.py

\`\`\`

\> 💡 This removes large intermediate files that are no longer needed, freeing up disk space before the next steps.

\---

\#\#\# Step 5: Invert Misregistration

\`\`\`bash

sh run\_files/run\_05\_invertMisreg

\`\`\`

\---

\#\#\# Step 6: Fine Resampling (Parallel)

\`\`\`bash

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_06\_fineResamp

\`\`\`

\---

\#\#\# Step 7: Grid Baseline

\`\`\`bash

sh run\_files/run\_07\_grid\_baseline

\`\`\`

\---

\#\#\# Step 8: Generate Interferograms (Parallel) 🎉

\`\`\`bash

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_08\_igram

\`\`\`

\> ⚠️ \*\*This is the longest step\!\*\* It may take hours. Consider running it inside a \`screen\` or \`tmux\` session so it continues even if you disconnect:

\>

\> \`\`\`bash

\> \# Start a persistent session

\> screen \-S insar\_processing

\>

\> \# Run the command

\> parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_08\_igram

\>

\> \# Detach from session (it keeps running): press Ctrl+A, then D

\> \# Reconnect later:

\> screen \-r insar\_processing

\> \`\`\`

\---

\#\# 6.3 Quick-Reference Command Summary

For easy copy-pasting, here's the complete sequence:

\`\`\`bash

\# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

\# ISCE2 PROCESSING PIPELINE — RUN IN ORDER

\# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

sh run\_files/run\_01\_reference

sh run\_files/run\_02\_focus\_split

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_04\_refineSecondaryTiming

poststep04\_cleanup.py

sh run\_files/run\_05\_invertMisreg

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_06\_fineResamp

sh run\_files/run\_07\_grid\_baseline

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_08\_igram

\`\`\`

\---

\#\# 6.4 Monitoring Progress

While processing is running, here's how to check on it:

\`\`\`bash

\# Check if processes are running

htop

\# Check the most recently modified files in your working directory

ls \-lt | head \-20

\# Check disk usage of your directory

du \-sh .

du \-sh \*/

\`\`\`

\---

\# 7\. Post-Processing & Quality Control

\---

\#\# 7.1 What to Check After Processing

After all run files complete, verify your results:

\`\`\`bash

\# Check that interferograms were created

ls interferograms/

\# Should see directories named like: 20070125\_20090626, 20070612\_20090626, etc.

\# Check inside one interferogram directory

ls interferograms/20070125\_20090626/

\# Should contain: .int, .cor, .unw files (interferogram, coherence, unwrapped phase)

\`\`\`

\---

\#\# 7.2 Key Output Files

| File Extension | Name | What It Shows |

|---------------|------|---------------|

| \`.int\` | Interferogram | Fringe pattern — raw phase difference between two dates |

| \`.cor\` | Coherence | Quality map (0 \= noise, 1 \= perfect signal) |

| \`.unw\` | Unwrapped phase | Phase converted to continuous values (needed for displacement calculation) |

\> 💡 \*\*What are "fringes"?\*\* In the interferogram (\`.int\`), you'll see colorful rainbow-like bands called fringes. Each complete color cycle (e.g., blue → green → red → blue) represents a specific amount of ground displacement (about 11.8 cm for ALOS L-band). More fringes \= more displacement.

\---

\#\# 7.3 ⚠️ Known Issue: FBS vs FBD Multilooking

\> \*\*Status: Under Investigation\*\*

\>

\> Currently, the \`stackStripMap.py\` command applies the same multilooking factors (\`-a 28 \-r 12\`) to both FBS and FBD data. This produces \~90 × 90 m pixels for FBS data but is \*\*not optimal for FBD data\*\*, which should use \`-r 6\` (6 range looks) instead of \`-r 12\`.

\>

\> | Mode | Azimuth Looks (\`-a\`) | Range Looks (\`-r\`) | Resulting Pixel Size |

\> |------|---------------------|--------------------|---------------------|

\> | FBS | 28 | 12 | \~90 × 90 m |

\> | FBD | 28 | \*\*6\*\* (should be) | \~90 × 90 m |

\>

\> \*\*For now:\*\* The pipeline uses \`-r 12\` for everything. A fix to handle mixed FBS/FBD stacks is planned.

\>

\> 🔍 \*\*References for this issue:\*\*

\> \- Page 20 of Francisco Delgado's ISCE2 Tutorial (see \[References\](\#9-references--resources))

\> \- Sandwell et al. (2008)

\> \- Werner et al. (2007)

\# 8\. Troubleshooting & FAQ

\---

\#\# ❓ Frequently Asked Questions

\#\#\# Q: How do I know which track and frame to process?

\*\*A:\*\* Your supervisor will assign you a track/frame pair. For LInOG, the primary track is \*\*448\*\* and frame is \*\*0290\*\*. You can find ALOS track/frame information at the \[ASF Data Search\](https://search.asf.alaska.edu/).

\#\#\# Q: What if my SSH connection drops during processing?

\*\*A:\*\* Use \`screen\` or \`tmux\` to keep processes running in the background:

\`\`\`bash

\# Start a session

screen \-S myprocess

\# Run your command

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_08\_igram

\# Detach: press Ctrl+A, then D

\# Reconnect later:

screen \-r myprocess

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Q: How do I know if a step completed successfully?

\*\*A:\*\* Check for error messages in the terminal output. You can also:

\`\`\`bash

\# Check if processes are still running

ps aux | grep python

\# Look at the last lines of a log file

tail \-50 isce.log

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Q: The DEM download fails — what do I do?

\*\*A:\*\*

1\. Check your \`.netrc\` file: \`cat \~/.netrc\`

2\. Check file permissions: \`ls \-la \~/.netrc\` (should show \`-rw-------\`)

3\. Test your credentials at \[urs.earthdata.nasa.gov\](https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov)

4\. \*\*Easiest fix:\*\* Just copy the pre-made DEM (see \[Section 4.1\](\#41-option-a-copy-the-pre-made-linog-dem-recommended))

\#\#\# Q: My \`parallel\` jobs are too slow or the server is unresponsive

\*\*A:\*\* Reduce the number of parallel jobs:

\`\`\`bash

\# Instead of 4 simultaneous jobs:

parallel \-j 4 \< run\_files/run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp

\# Try 2:

parallel \-j 2 \< run\_files/run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp

\# Or run one at a time:

parallel \-j 1 \< run\_files/run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Q: How do I rerun a single failed step?

\*\*A:\*\* You can edit the run file to include only the failed commands, or run the specific command manually. Check the run file with:

\`\`\`bash

cat run\_files/run\_03\_geo2rdr\_coarseResamp

\# Find the specific line that failed and run just that line

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Q: I'm stuck in Vim and can't get out\!

\*\*A:\*\* Press \`Esc\` a few times, then type \`:q\!\` and press \`Enter\`. This force-quits without saving. You can always reopen the file and start over.

\---

\#\# 🐛 Common Errors

| Error | Likely Cause | Fix |

|-------|-------------|-----|

| \`command not found: stackStripMap.py\` | ISCE2 not loaded | Activate conda env: \`conda activate isce2\` |

| \`command not found: find\_alos.sh\` | \`\~/bin\` not in PATH | Run \`source \~/.bashrc\` or add to PATH |

| \`Permission denied\` | File not executable | Run \`chmod \+x \~/bin/scriptname.sh\` |

| \`No such file or directory: SLC/\` | Haven't unpacked data yet | Complete \[Pre-Stack Processing\](\#3-pre-stack-processing) first |

| \`DEM file not found\` | DEM not in expected location | Check \`ls DEM/\` and verify filename in your command |

| \`urllib.error.HTTPError: 401\` | Bad NASA credentials | Fix your \`\~/.netrc\` file |

| \`Killed\` or \`MemoryError\` | Server ran out of RAM | Reduce \`parallel \-j\` count or wait for other users to finish |

| \`E212: Can't open file for writing\` | No write permission (Vim) | Check \`ls \-la filename\` — use \`chmod\` or \`sudo\` if needed |

\#\# 📝 Glossary

| Term | Definition |

|------|-----------|

| \*\*ALOS\*\* | Advanced Land Observing Satellite (Japanese satellite, also called "Daichi") |

| \*\*PALSAR\*\* | Phased Array type L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (the radar instrument on ALOS) |

| \*\*InSAR\*\* | Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar — technique to measure ground deformation |

| \*\*SLC\*\* | Single Look Complex — radar image with amplitude and phase information |

| \*\*DEM\*\* | Digital Elevation Model — grid of ground surface heights |

| \*\*SRTM\*\* | Shuttle Radar Topography Mission — source of a widely-used global DEM |

| \*\*FBS\*\* | Fine Beam Single polarization mode (ALOS PALSAR) |

| \*\*FBD\*\* | Fine Beam Dual polarization mode (ALOS PALSAR) |

| \*\*Baseline\*\* | Distance between satellite positions for two acquisitions |

| \*\*Interferogram\*\* | Map of phase differences between two radar images |

| \*\*Coherence\*\* | Measure of signal quality (0 \= pure noise, 1 \= perfect) |

| \*\*Phase unwrapping\*\* | Converting wrapped (cyclic) phase to continuous displacement values |

| \*\*Geocoding\*\* | Mapping radar coordinates to geographic (lat/lon) coordinates |

| \*\*Multilooking\*\* | Spatial averaging to reduce noise at the cost of resolution |

| \*\*SNAPHU\*\* | Statistical-Cost, Network-Flow Algorithm for Phase Unwrapping |

| \*\*ISCE2\*\* | InSAR Scientific Computing Environment version 2 (NASA JPL software) |

| \*\*Symlink\*\* | Symbolic link — a file that points to another file (like a shortcut) |

| \*\*SSH\*\* | Secure Shell — protocol for securely connecting to remote servers |

| \*\*PATH\*\* | Environment variable listing directories where the system looks for programs |

| \*\*Vim\*\* | A powerful terminal-based text editor available on all Unix/Linux systems |

GEMINI:

That "event not found" error happened because Bash interprets the exclamation point `!` in `#!/bin/bash` as a **History Expansion** character. When using `echo` with double quotes, it tries to find a previous command starting with `/bin/bash`.

To fix this while maintaining your workflow, we will use **single quotes** for the shebang line and then use **Vim** to verify the script.

ARIEL:

(isce2) arieln@felix:/eggraid/home/arieln/projects/linog/insar/p448/f310$ \# Create a symlink so 'data' points to 'raw'

ln \-s raw data 2\>&1 | tee \-a logs/01\_find\_alos.log.v1

this is my mintpy documentation for my fbs stack processing for path 448 frame 0290 

\# MintPy Processing 

\*\*ALOS-1 FBD (L-band) InSAR Time-Series Analysis\*\*  

\*\*Processing Stack:\*\* ISCE2 stripmapStack \+ MintPy  

\*\*Temporal Coverage:\*\* 2007-06-21 to 2010-09-29 (12 acquisitions, 34 interferograms)  

\*\*Last Updated:\*\* February 10, 2026

\---

\#\# Table of Contents

\- \[Prerequisites\](\#prerequisites)

\- \[Phase 1: Data Ingestion (Steps 0-2)\](\#phase-1-data-ingestion-steps-0-2)

\- \[Phase 2: Network Inversion & Quality (Steps 3-6)\](\#phase-2-network-inversion--quality-steps-3-6)

\- \[Phase 3: Atmospheric & Orbital Corrections (Steps 7-9)\](\#phase-3-atmospheric--orbital-corrections-steps-7-9)

\- \[Phase 4: Final Products (Steps 10-12)\](\#phase-4-final-products-steps-10-12)

\- \[Appendix: Configuration Summary\](\#appendix-configuration-summary)

\---

\#\# Prerequisites

\#\#\# Software Environment

\`\`\`bash

\# Activate ISCE2/MintPy conda environment

conda activate isce2

\# Verify installations

prep\_isce.py \--version

smallbaselineApp.py \--help

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Directory Structure

\`\`\`

linog/insar/448/0290/

├── merged/SLC/20090626/referenceShelve/data.dat  \# ISCE metadata

├── baselines/                                     \# Baseline directory

├── Igrams/\*/filt\_\*.unw                           \# Unwrapped interferograms

├── geom\_reference/                               \# Geometry files

└── mintpy/                                        \# Processing directory (create this)

\`\`\`

\#\#\# Key Files Required

\- \[smallbaselineApp\](\#smallbaselineApp)

\- ISCE stripmapStack outputs (interferograms, coherence, geometry)

\---

\#\# Phase 1: Data Ingestion (Steps 0-2)

\#\#\# \*\*Step 0: Load Data\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

MintPy reads ISCE metadata (baselines, orbital state vectors, geometry) to construct a unified HDF5 stack. For \`stripmapStack\`, metadata files must be manually prepared using \`prep\_isce.py\` to avoid \`KeyError\` failures.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

\`\`\`

KeyError: 'STARTING\_RANGE'

ValueError: Could not load wrapped interferograms

\`\`\`

\*\*Cause:\*\* ISCE \`stripmapStack\` does not auto-generate \`.rsc\` resource files expected by MintPy. Missing metadata prevents stack construction.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Run \`prep\_isce.py\` \*\*before\*\* loading data to generate missing metadata headers.

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# set variable for ref date

ref\_date=20091111

\# Navigate to mintpy directory

cd \~/projects/linog/insar/448/0290/mintpy

\# 1\. Generate ISCE metadata files

prep\_isce.py \-m ../merged/SLC/$ref\_date/referenceShelve/data.dat \\

             \-g ../geom\_reference \\

             \-b ../baselines \\

             \-f "../Igrams/\*/filt\_\*.unw"

\# 2\. Generate mintpy config file

smallbaselineApp.py \-g

\# 3\. Configure smallbaselineApp.cfg using the sed commands below

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.metaFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.metaFile \= ../merged/SLC/$ref\_date/referenceShelve/data.dat|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.baselineDir.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.baselineDir \= ../baselines|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.intFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.intFile \= no|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.demFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.demFile \= ../geom\_reference/hgt.rdr|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.lookupYFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.lookupYFile \= ../geom\_reference/lat.rdr|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.lookupXFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.lookupXFile \= ../geom\_reference/lon.rdr|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.incAngleFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.incAngleFile \= ../geom\_reference/los.rdr|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.shadowMaskFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.shadowMaskFile \= ../geom\_reference/shadowMask.rdr|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

sed \-i 's|mintpy.load.waterMaskFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.load.waterMaskFile \= ../geom\_reference/waterMask.rdr|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 4\. Remove any failed HDF5 attempts

rm \-f inputs/ifgramStack.h5

\# 4\. Load data with logging

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep load\_data | tee log\_01\_load\_data.txt

\# 5\. Sanity check: Generate quick-look images

view.py inputs/ifgramStack.h5 unwrapPhase \--nodisplay \--save

view.py inputs/ifgramStack.h5 coherence \--nodisplay \--save

\# 6\. Transfer to local machine for inspection

\# (Run on LOCAL machine)

rsync \-avz user@server:/path/to/mintpy/\*.png .

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# Additional \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.load.processor       \= isce

mintpy.load.metaFile        \= ../merged/SLC/$ref\_date/referenceShelve/data.dat

mintpy.load.baselineDir     \= ../baselines

mintpy.load.unwFile         \= ../Igrams/\*/filt\_\*.unw

mintpy.load.corFile         \= ../Igrams/\*/filt\_\*.cor

mintpy.load.connCompFile    \= ../Igrams/\*/filt\_\*.unw.conncomp

mintpy.load.intFile         \= no  \# Disabled to bypass ValueError

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*File Created:\*\* \`inputs/ifgramStack.h5\` (658 × 773 pixels, 34 pairs)

\- \*\*Coherence Range:\*\* 0.00 \- 1.00 (expected for ALOS-1 FBD over vegetation)

\- \*\*Visual Check:\*\* \`unwrapPhase.png\` shows consistent fringes; \`coherence.png\` reveals high-quality pairs (e.g., 20080808\_20080923)

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: unwrapPhase.png \- Grid of 34 interferograms showing phase gradients\]\*\*  

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: coherence.png \- Grid showing decorrelation patterns\]\*\*

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 1: Network Construction\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Visualize interferometric network connectivity. High redundancy (multiple connections per date) ensures robust time-series inversion.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

\`\`\`

RuntimeWarning: Mean of empty slice

\`\`\`

\*\*Cause:\*\* Default \`waterMask.h5\` failed to download from USGS, leaving an empty mask that zeroed out the entire study area.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Generate a \*\*coherence-based mask\*\* directly from \`ifgramStack.h5\` instead of relying on external water body files.

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Create mask from coherence (threshold \= 0.4)

generate\_mask.py inputs/ifgramStack.h5 \--nonzero \-m 0.4 \-o waterMask.h5

\# 2\. Update configuration

sed \-i 's|mintpy.network.maskFile.\*=.\*|mintpy.network.maskFile \= waterMask.h5|' smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 3\. Clean up failed average file

rm \-f coherenceSpatialAvg.txt

\# 4\. Run network modification

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep modify\_network | tee log\_02\_modify\_network.txt

\# 5\. Generate network plots

plot\_network.py inputs/ifgramStack.h5 \--save

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.network.coherenceBased  \= auto  \# Disabled (using minCoherence threshold instead)

mintpy.network.minCoherence    \= 0.7

mintpy.network.keepMinSpanTree \= auto

mintpy.network.maskFile        \= waterMask.h5

mintpy.network.aoiYX           \= 200:300,200:300  \# Area of interest for coherence calculation

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Network Statistics:\*\*

  \- Acquisitions: 12

  \- Interferograms kept: 34

  \- Average coherence: 0.71 (range: 0.4142 \- 0.9918)

  \- Max perpendicular baseline: 1492.4 m

  \- Max temporal baseline: 1196 days

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: network.pdf \- Baseline-time plot showing fully connected graph\]\*\*  

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: coherenceMatrix.pdf \- Grid showing pair-wise coherence values\]\*\*  

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: pbaseHistory.pdf \- Perpendicular baseline evolution\]\*\*

\#\# Phase 2: Network Inversion & Quality (Steps 3-6)

\#\#\# \*\*Step 3: Reference Point Selection\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Select a spatially stable pixel (high coherence, minimal deformation) to serve as the "zero displacement" anchor for all interferograms.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

No issues encountered—MintPy's automatic selection algorithm worked correctly with the coherence-based mask.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

MintPy automatically selected pixel (586, 100\) based on highest temporal coherence. Manual verification confirmed suitability.

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Select reference point

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep reference\_point | tee log\_03\_reference\_point.txt

\# 2\. Verify reference point attributes

info.py inputs/ifgramStack.h5 | grep REF

\# 3\. Check coherence value at reference point

python \<\< EOF

import h5py

with h5py.File('avgSpatialCoh.h5', 'r') as f:

    value \= f\['coherence'\]\[586, 100\]

    print(f"Average Coherence at (586, 100): {value:.4f}")

EOF

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.reference.yx            \= auto   \# Auto-selected (586, 100\)

mintpy.reference.lalo          \= auto   

mintpy.reference.maskFile      \= auto   \# Uses maskConnComp.h5

mintpy.reference.coherenceFile \= auto   \# Uses avgSpatialCoh.h5

mintpy.reference.minCoherence  \= auto   \# 0.85 threshold

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Selected Pixel:\*\* (586, 100\) → Y: 586, X: 100

\- \*\*Coherence Value:\*\* 0.8580 (well above 0.85 threshold)

\- \*\*Geographic Location:\*\* Bottom-left of study area, on stable land

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: ref\_point\_check.png \- Coherence map with reference point marked\]\*\*

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 4: Quick Overview\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Perform phase closure analysis to identify unwrapping errors. Examines 38 interferogram triplets to detect non-zero integer ambiguities.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

No errors—step completed in 0.1 seconds.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Not applicable (step succeeded).

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Run quick overview

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep quick\_overview | tee log\_04\_quick\_overview.txt

\# 2\. View phase closure errors

view.py numTriNonzeroIntAmbiguity.h5 \--nodisplay \--save

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Triplets Analyzed:\*\* 38

\- \*\*File Created:\*\* \`numTriNonzeroIntAmbiguity.h5\` (phase closure map)

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: numTriNonzeroIntAmbiguity.png \- Map showing unwrapping error distribution\]\*\*

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 5: Correct Unwrapping Errors\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Use phase closure to identify and correct 2π integer ambiguities in unwrapped interferograms.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

\`\`\`

Found NO common regions with size \>= 2500 pixels

\`\`\`

\*\*Cause:\*\* Default \`connCompMinArea \= 2500\` too restrictive for fragmented coherence over tropical vegetation.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Lower minimum area threshold to 100 pixels to allow correction on smaller coherent patches.

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Enable phase closure correction

sed \-i 's/.\*mintpy.unwrapError.method.\*/mintpy.unwrapError.method \= phase\_closure/' smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 2\. Lower minimum area threshold

sed \-i 's/.\*mintpy.unwrapError.connCompMinArea.\*/mintpy.unwrapError.connCompMinArea \= 100/' smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 3\. Verify changes

grep \-E "unwrapError\\.(method|connCompMinArea)" smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 4\. Run correction

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep correct\_unwrap\_error | tee log\_05\_correct\_unwrap\_error.txt

\# 5\. View corrected regions

view.py common\_region\_sample.png \--nodisplay \--save

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.unwrapError.method          \= phase\_closure

mintpy.unwrapError.waterMaskFile   \= auto

mintpy.unwrapError.connCompMinArea \= 100  \# Reduced from 2500

mintpy.unwrapError.numSample       \= auto

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Common Regions Found:\*\* 1 (primary coherent landmass)

\- \*\*Correction Method:\*\* L1-norm regularized least squares

\- \*\*New Dataset:\*\* \`unwrapPhase\_phaseClosure\` created in \`ifgramStack.h5\`

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: common\_region\_sample.png \- Highlighted correction region\]\*\*

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 6: Network Inversion\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Invert 34 interferograms into a continuous displacement time-series using Weighted Least Squares (WLS). Coherence values weight each pixel's contribution.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue (First Attempt)\*\*

\`\`\`

Found 863 valid pixels (0.2% of total)

After masking with temporal coherence \> 0.7: 584 pixels

\`\`\`

\*\*Cause:\*\* Overly aggressive masking from \`avgSpatialCoh.h5\` and high \`minTempCoh\` threshold.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

1\. Remove restrictive masks (\`avgSpatialCoh.h5\`, \`maskConnComp.h5\`)

2\. Lower temporal coherence threshold from 0.7 to 0.5

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Remove restrictive masks

rm \-f avgSpatialCoh.h5 maskConnComp.h5

\# 2\. Lower temporal coherence threshold

sed \-i 's/.\*mintpy.networkInversion.minTempCoh.\*/mintpy.networkInversion.minTempCoh \= 0.5/' smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 3\. Run inversion

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep invert\_network | tee log\_06\_invert\_network.txt

\# 4\. View temporal coherence

view.py temporalCoherence.h5 \--mask maskTempCoh.h5 \--nodisplay \--save \-o temporalCoherence\_masked.png

\# 5\. View raw velocity

view.py velocity.h5 \--mask maskTempCoh.h5 \--nodisplay \--save \-o velocity\_pre\_correction.png

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.networkInversion.weightFunc      \= auto  \# Uses variance

mintpy.networkInversion.waterMaskFile   \= auto

mintpy.networkInversion.minNormVelocity \= auto

mintpy.networkInversion.maskDataset     \= no

mintpy.networkInversion.minTempCoh      \= 0.5   \# Lowered from 0.7

mintpy.networkInversion.minNumPixel     \= auto

mintpy.networkInversion.shadowMask      \= auto

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Total Pixels Inverted:\*\* 508,633 (100% of image)

\- \*\*Reliable Pixels (TempCoh \> 0.5):\*\* 113,518 (22.3%)

\- \*\*Reference Pixel TempCoh:\*\* 1.0 (as expected)

\- \*\*Processing Time:\*\* 54.8 seconds

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: temporalCoherence\_masked.png \- 113k reliable pixels shown in white\]\*\*  

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: velocity\_pre\_correction.png \- Raw velocity showing orbital ramps\]\*\*

\---

\#\# Phase 3: Atmospheric & Orbital Corrections (Steps 7-9)

\#\#\# \*\*Step 7: Tropospheric Correction\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Remove stratified tropospheric delay correlated with topography. Water vapor slows radar waves, creating false deformation signals that mimic terrain.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

\`\`\`

ZeroDivisionError in pyaps module

HTTP Error 500: Internal Server Error (ERA5 server)

\`\`\`

\*\*Cause:\*\* Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) server failure prevented ERA5 model download for 2007-2011 dates.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Switch from \`pyaps\` (requires external weather models) to \`height\_correlation\` (empirical, uses only existing geometry).

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Switch to height\_correlation method

sed \-i 's/.\*mintpy.troposphericDelay.method.\*/mintpy.troposphericDelay.method \= height\_correlation/' smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 2\. Run correction

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep correct\_troposphere | tee log\_07\_correct\_troposphere.txt

\# 3\. View corrected time-series

view.py timeseries\_tropHgt.h5 \--nodisplay \--save \-o tropo\_delay.png

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.troposphericDelay.method         \= height\_correlation

mintpy.troposphericDelay.polyOrder      \= auto  \# 1st order (linear)

mintpy.troposphericDelay.looks          \= auto  \# 8x multilooking for estimation

mintpy.troposphericDelay.minCorrelation \= auto  \# 0.0 threshold

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Average Correlation:\*\* 0.50 (strong topographic relationship)

\- \*\*Best Dates:\*\* 20100629 (R=0.64), 20100814 (R=0.61)

\- \*\*Worst Dates:\*\* 20071106 (R=-0.44, inverse moisture pattern)

\- \*\*Processing Time:\*\* 0.2 seconds

\- \*\*New File:\*\* \`timeseries\_tropHgt.h5\`

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: tropo\_delay.png \- Time-series showing reduced topographic correlation\]\*\*

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 8: Orbital Deramping\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Remove long-wavelength orbital errors that manifest as linear/quadratic "ramps" across the scene. Critical for ALOS-1 due to poor orbit accuracy.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue (First Attempt)\*\*

\`\`\`

Massive 80 cm displacement gradient in 2010-09-29 acquisition

Linear deramp insufficient to remove complex warping

\`\`\`

\*\*Cause:\*\* ALOS-1 orbital state vectors degraded over time; ionospheric noise combined with orbital error created non-linear phase surface.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Upgrade from \`linear\` to \`quadratic\` deramp to fit complex 2D curved surface.

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Remove all existing deramp settings

sed \-i '/mintpy.deramp/d' smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 2\. Set quadratic deramp

echo 'mintpy.deramp \= quadratic' \>\> smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 3\. Verify configuration

grep "mintpy.deramp" smallbaselineApp.cfg

\# 4\. Remove old linear output

rm \-f timeseries\_tropHgt\_ramp.h5

\# 5\. Run quadratic deramp

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep deramp | tee log\_08\_deramp\_quad.txt

\# 6\. View flattened time-series

view.py timeseries\_tropHgt\_ramp.h5 \--nodisplay \--save \-o timeseries\_deramped\_quad.png

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.deramp          \= quadratic  \# Upgraded from 'linear'

mintpy.deramp.maskFile \= auto       \# Uses maskTempCoh.h5

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Ramp Model:\*\* 2D quadratic polynomial (6 parameters per date)

\- \*\*80 cm Gradient:\*\* Successfully neutralized in 2010-09-29

\- \*\*Processing Time:\*\* \< 1 second

\- \*\*New File:\*\* \`timeseries\_tropHgt\_ramp.h5\`

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: timeseries\_deramped\_quad.png \- Time-series after quadratic deramping\]\*\*

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 9: Topographic Residual Correction\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Estimate and remove DEM errors by exploiting correlation between phase and perpendicular baseline. Small DEM inaccuracies create "fake" displacement proportional to baseline.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

No errors—step automatically re-ran after quadratic deramp update.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Not applicable (step succeeded after providing clean quadratic input).

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Run topographic correction (automatically uses quadratic deramped data)

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep correct\_topography | tee log\_09\_correct\_topography.txt

\# 2\. View final cleaned time-series

view.py timeseries\_tropHgt\_ramp\_demErr.h5 \--nodisplay \--save \-o timeseries\_final\_cleaned.png

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.topographicResidual                   \= yes

mintpy.topographicResidual.polyOrder         \= auto  \# 2nd order temporal model

mintpy.topographicResidual.phaseVelocity     \= auto  \# Uses phase (not velocity)

mintpy.topographicResidual.stepDate          \= auto

mintpy.topographicResidual.excludeDate       \= auto

mintpy.topographicResidual.pixelwiseGeometry \= auto  \# Uses pixel-wise inc/slant range

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*DEM Error Range:\*\* \-50 to \+50 meters (typical for SRTM over rugged terrain)

\- \*\*Processing Time:\*\* 32.1 seconds (508,633 pixels)

\- \*\*New File:\*\* \`timeseries\_tropHgt\_ramp\_demErr.h5\` (final cleaned time-series)

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: timeseries\_final\_cleaned.png \- Time-series with all corrections applied\]\*\*

\---

\#\# Phase 4: Final Products (Steps 10-12)

\#\#\# \*\*Step 10: Reference Date\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Anchor time-series to a specific date (first acquisition by default). All displacement values become relative to this epoch.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

No issues—step completed instantly.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Not applicable (step succeeded).

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Set reference date (uses first date: 20070621\)

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep reference\_date

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.reference.date \= auto  \# Uses first date (20070621)

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Reference Date:\*\* 2007-06-21

\- \*\*All Dates Shifted:\*\* Displacement on 2007-06-21 \= 0.0 meters for all pixels

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 11: Velocity Estimation\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Fit linear model to time-series to estimate average deformation rate (m/year). Uses ordinary least squares with optional uncertainty quantification.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

No issues—inversion completed in 0.2 seconds.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Not applicable (step succeeded).

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Estimate velocity

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep velocity | tee log\_11\_velocity\_final.txt

\# 2\. View velocity map

view.py velocity.h5 \--mask maskTempCoh.h5 \--nodisplay \--save \-o velocity\_final.png

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.timeFunc.polynomial \= 1      \# Linear model (velocity only)

mintpy.timeFunc.periodic   \= auto   \# No seasonal terms

mintpy.timeFunc.stepDate   \= auto   \# No coseismic steps

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Velocity Range:\*\* \-0.10 to \+0.26 m/year (-10 to \+26 cm/year)

\- \*\*Velocity Std Dev:\*\* \< 0.01 m/year (very low uncertainty)

\- \*\*Deformation Pattern:\*\* Distinct blue cluster (uplift/movement toward satellite) on western side

\- \*\*Files Created:\*\* \`velocity.h5\`, \`velocityStd.h5\`, \`residue.h5\`

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: velocity\_final.png \- Four-panel plot showing velocity, uncertainty, intercept, residue\]\*\*

\---

\#\#\# \*\*Step 12: Geocoding & Export\*\*

\#\#\#\# \*\*Description\*\*

Transform results from radar coordinates (range/azimuth) to geographic coordinates (lat/lon). Generate visualization products for GIS and Google Earth.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Issue\*\*

No issues—geocoding completed successfully.

\#\#\#\# \*\*The Solution\*\*

Not applicable (step succeeded).

\#\#\#\# \*\*Code\*\*

\`\`\`bash

\# 1\. Geocode all products

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep geocode

\# 2\. Generate Google Earth KMZ

smallbaselineApp.py smallbaselineApp.cfg \--dostep google\_earth

\# 3\. Create hillshade overlay

view.py geo/geo\_velocity.h5 velocity \\

    \--mask geo/geo\_maskTempCoh.h5 \\

    \-d geo/geo\_geometryRadar.h5 \\

    \--shade-exag 0.05 \\

    \--nodisplay \--save \\

    \-o velocity\_on\_hillshade.png \\

    \--dpi 300

\# 4\. Export Shapefile for QGIS

save\_qgis.py geo/geo\_timeseries\_tropHgt\_ramp\_demErr.h5 \\

    \-g geo/geo\_geometryRadar.h5 \\

    \-o velocity\_points\_shp

\# 5\. Download products to local machine

\# (Run on LOCAL machine)

scp \-r user@server:/path/to/mintpy/geo/\*.{kmz,h5} .

scp \-r user@server:/path/to/mintpy/velocity\_on\_hillshade.png .

scp \-r user@server:/path/to/mintpy/velocity\_points\_shp .

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Config Settings\*\*

\`\`\`cfg

mintpy.geocode              \= auto  \# Enabled (yes)

mintpy.geocode.SNWE         \= auto  \# Auto-determined extent

mintpy.geocode.laloStep     \= auto  \# \~90m resolution (0.0008°)

mintpy.geocode.interpMethod \= auto  \# Nearest neighbor

mintpy.save.kmz             \= yes   \# Generate KMZ

\`\`\`

\#\#\#\# \*\*Results\*\*

\- \*\*Geographic Extent:\*\* 15.01°N \- 15.65°N, 120.86°E \- 121.60°E

\- \*\*Resolution:\*\* 0.0008° (\~90 meters)

\- \*\*Grid Size:\*\* 794 rows × 887 columns

\- \*\*Files Created:\*\*

  \- \`geo/geo\_velocity.h5\` (geocoded velocity)

  \- \`geo/geo\_velocity.kmz\` (Google Earth file, 600 DPI)

  \- \`geo/geo\_geometryRadar.h5\` (DEM, incidence angle)

  \- \`velocity\_points\_shp/\` (Shapefile with 116,786 points)

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: velocity\_geocoded\_final.png \- Velocity map with lat/lon axes and 20km scale bar\]\*\*  

\*\*\[INSERT IMAGE: velocity\_on\_hillshade.png \- Velocity draped over terrain hillshade\]\*\*

\#\# Appendix: Configuration Summary

\#\#\# Critical Parameters for LInOG Processing

\#\# smallbaselineApp

\`\`\`cfg

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Load Data \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.load.processor       \= isce

mintpy.load.intFile         \= no  \# Disable wrapped interferograms

mintpy.multilook.ystep      \= 1   \# No multilooking

mintpy.multilook.xstep      \= 1

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Network Modification \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.network.minCoherence    \= 0.7

mintpy.network.keepMinSpanTree \= auto

mintpy.network.maskFile        \= waterMask.h5

mintpy.network.aoiYX           \= 200:300,200:300

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Reference Point \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.reference.yx           \= auto  \# Auto-selected (586, 100\)

mintpy.reference.minCoherence \= auto  \# 0.85 threshold

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Unwrap Error Correction \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.unwrapError.method          \= phase\_closure

mintpy.unwrapError.connCompMinArea \= 100  \# Lowered from default 2500

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Network Inversion \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.networkInversion.weightFunc      \= auto  \# Variance weighting

mintpy.networkInversion.minTempCoh      \= 0.5   \# Lowered from 0.7

mintpy.networkInversion.minNormVelocity \= auto

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Tropospheric Correction \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.troposphericDelay.method \= height\_correlation  \# Changed from pyaps

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Orbital Deramping \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.deramp          \= quadratic  \# Upgraded from linear

mintpy.deramp.maskFile \= auto

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Topographic Correction \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.topographicResidual                   \= yes

mintpy.topographicResidual.polyOrder         \= auto

mintpy.topographicResidual.pixelwiseGeometry \= auto

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Velocity Estimation \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.timeFunc.polynomial \= 1  \# Linear velocity only

\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\# Geocoding \#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#\#

mintpy.geocode.laloStep \= auto  \# \~90m resolution

mintpy.save.kmz         \= yes

import numpy as np, h5py, os, zipfile, sys

from datetime import datetime

def make\_interactive\_v7(frame\_dir, ts\_file, out\_name, delivery\_folder, frame\_label, process\_label):

    geo\_dir \= os.path.join(frame\_dir, 'mintpy', 'geo')

    ts\_path \= os.path.join(geo\_dir, ts\_file)

    vel\_path \= os.path.join(geo\_dir, 'geo\_velocity.h5')

    mask\_path \= os.path.join(geo\_dir, 'geo\_maskTempCoh.h5')

    delivery\_path \= os.path.join(geo\_dir, delivery\_folder)

    if not os.path.exists(ts\_path):

        print(f"Skipping: {ts\_path} not found.")

        return

    with h5py.File(ts\_path, 'r') as f:

        ts \= f\['timeseries'\]\[:\] \* 100

        dates \= \[d.decode() for d in f\['date'\]\[:\]\]

        a \= dict(f.attrs)

        yf, xf, ys, xs \= float(a\['Y\_FIRST'\]), float(a\['X\_FIRST'\]), float(a\['Y\_STEP'\]), float(a\['X\_STEP'\])

    with h5py.File(vel\_path, 'r') as f:

        vel \= f\['velocity'\]\[:\] \* 100

        vs\_map \= f\['velocityStd'\]\[:\] \* 100

    with h5py.File(mask\_path, 'r') as f:

        mask \= f\['mask'\]\[:\].astype(bool)

    dos \= \[datetime.strptime(d, '%Y%m%d') for d in dates\]

    vmin, vmax \= \-10, 10

    def v2c(v):

        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

        cm \= plt.cm.jet

        n \= np.clip((v \- vmin) / (vmax \- vmin), 0, 1\)

        r, g, b, \_ \= cm(n)

        return 'ff{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}'.format(int(b\*255), int(g\*255), int(r\*255))

    pms \= \[\]

    print(f"Building KMZ: {frame\_label} ({process\_label})...")

    for r in range(0, ts.shape\[1\], 5):

        for c in range(0, ts.shape\[2\], 5):

            if not mask\[r,c\] or np.isnan(vel\[r,c\]): continue

            la, lo, v, vs \= yf+ys\*r, xf+xs\*c, vel\[r,c\], vs\_map\[r,c\]

            rows \= \[f"\[new Date({d.year},{d.month-1},{d.day}),{ts\[i,r,c\]:.2f}\]" for i, d in enumerate(dos)\]

            table\_rows \= "".join(\[f"\<tr\>\<td style='border:1px solid \#ddd; padding:2px;'\>{d.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}\</td\>\<td style='border:1px solid \#ddd;'\>{ts\[i,r,c\]:.2f}\</td\>\</tr\>" for i, d in enumerate(dos)\])

            bl \= f'''\<\!\[CDATA\[

            \<div style="width:480px; font-family:Arial; font-size:12px; color:\#333;"\>

                \<h3 style="margin:0 0 5px 0;"\>LInOG {frame\_label} ({process\_label})\</h3\>

                \<div style="margin-bottom:10px;"\>\<b\>Velocity:\</b\> {v:.2f} \+/- {vs:.2f} cm/yr\</div\>

                \<div id="chart\_container\_{r}\_{c}" style="width:100%; height:220px; border:1px solid \#eee; background:\#fcfcfc;"\>

                    \<div style="padding:80px 0; text-align:center; color:\#999;"\>Loading Time-Series...\</div\>

                \</div\>

                \<div style="margin-top:10px; max-height:130px; overflow-y:auto; border:1px solid \#ddd;"\>

                    \<table style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; text-align:center;"\>

                        \<thead style="background:\#eee; position:sticky; top:0;"\>

                            \<tr\>\<th style="padding:4px; border:1px solid \#ddd;"\>Date\</th\>\<th style="padding:4px; border:1px solid \#ddd;"\>Disp (cm)\</th\>\</tr\>

                        \</thead\>

                        \<tbody\>{table\_rows}\</tbody\>

                    \</table\>

                \</div\>

                \<script type="text/javascript" src="https://www.gstatic.com/charts/loader.js"\>\</script\>

                \<script type="text/javascript"\>

                    (function() {{

                        function draw() {{

                            var data \= new google.visualization.DataTable();

                            data.addColumn('date', 'Date');

                            data.addColumn('number', 'Displacement (cm)');

                            data.addRows(\[{",".join(rows)}\]);

                            var options \= {{

                                title: 'Displacement History',

                                legend: {{ position: 'none' }},

                                pointSize: 6,

                                colors: \['\#008080'\],

                                chartArea: {{width: '85%', height: '75%'}},

                                vAxis: {{ title: 'cm', gridlines: {{color: '\#f0f0f0'}} }},

                                hAxis: {{ format: 'MMM yyyy' }}

                            }};

                            var container \= document.getElementById('chart\_container\_{r}\_{c}');

                            if(container) {{

                                var chart \= new google.visualization.ScatterChart(container);

                                chart.draw(data, options);

                            }}

                        }}

                        if (typeof google \!== 'undefined' && google.charts) {{

                            if (\!google.visualization || \!google.visualization.ScatterChart) {{

                                google.charts.load('current', {{'packages':\['corechart'\]}});

                                google.charts.setOnLoadCallback(draw);

                            }} else {{

                                draw();

                            }}

                        }}

                    }})();

                \</script\>

            \</div\>\]\]\>'''

            pms.append(f'''\<Placemark\>

                \<description\>{bl}\</description\>

                \<Style\>

                    \<IconStyle\>

                        \<color\>{v2c(v)}\</color\>

                        \<scale\>0.5\</scale\>

                        \<Icon\>\<href\>http://maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/shapes/shaded\_dot.png\</href\>\</Icon\>

                    \</IconStyle\>

                \</Style\>

                \<Point\>\<coordinates\>{lo:.6f},{la:.6f},0\</coordinates\>\</Point\>

            \</Placemark\>''')

    kml \= f'\<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?\>\<kml xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2"\>\<Document\>\<name\>{out\_name}\</name\>{chr(10).join(pms)}\</Document\>\</kml\>'

    os.makedirs(delivery\_path, exist\_ok=True)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(os.path.join(delivery\_path, out\_name), "w", zipfile.ZIP\_DEFLATED) as zf:

        zf.writestr("doc.kml", kml)

    print(f"✅ Created: {out\_name}")

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":

    \]

geocode.py velocity_demErr.h5 timeseries_demErr.h5 -l inputs/geometryRadar.h5 -t smallbaselineApp.cfg --outdir geo --update 2>&1 | tee -a ../logs/22_demErr_only_v1.log

## P447 F0300 MintPy Error Log — Jun 7, 2026

**Context:** P447 (ALOS-1 PALSAR, Path 447, Central Luzon), Frame F0300, reference date 20090309, 38 interferometric pairs. Processing on felix server, `isce2` conda env, MintPy 1.6.2. Three errors encountered and resolved during the first full MintPy pipeline run. All three share a common root: `waterMask.rdr` in the P447 ISCE2 `geom_reference/` directory is an all-zero binary raster.

---

### M1: `modify_network` — `ValueError: Invalid NaN value found in kept pairs for Bperp or coherence`

**Traceback signature:**
```
ValueError: Invalid NaN value found in kept pairs for Bperp or coherence.
```

**Root cause:** During `load_data`, MintPy loads `waterMask.rdr` into `geometryRadar.h5['waterMask']`. Because the raster is all-zero, `modify_network` generates `waterMask.h5` by ANDing the all-zero dataset with a lat/lon non-zero check. Lat/lon were valid (15.50–16.14 N, 121.30–122.04 E), but the AND of any valid mask with all-zero is still all-zero (0/511924 valid). `plot_network` then computed spatial mean coherence over an empty mask, producing all NaN, then crashed with `ValueError`.

**Fix:**
1. Patch `geometryRadar.h5['waterMask']` to all-ones:
```python
import h5py, numpy as np
with h5py.File('inputs/geometryRadar.h5', 'a') as f:
    f['waterMask'][:] = np.ones_like(f['waterMask'][:])
```
2. Remove stale derived files: `rm waterMask.h5 coherenceSpatialAvg.txt`
3. In `smallbaselineApp.cfg`: `mintpy.load.waterMaskFile = no`
4. Re-run `modify_network`.

**Automated in batch script v2.0:** `heal_watermask_patch()` runs after every successful `load_data`. Detects all-zero `geometryRadar.h5['waterMask']`, patches it to all-ones, removes stale files. Auto-heal error catalog entry: `WATERMASK_NAN`.

---

### M2: `correct_unwrap_error` — `ValueError: input reference point is NOT included in the connectComponent`

**Traceback signature:**
```
ValueError: input reference point is NOT included in the connectComponent.
```

**Root cause:** `maskConnComp.h5` is the intersection of all 38 SNAPHU connected component masks. Rainy-season interferogram pairs had zero valid connected components (decorrelated pixels); their intersection is 0/511924 valid pixels. The bridging algorithm requires a non-empty `maskConnComp` to anchor the reference point. Step crashed at pair 20/38 with no valid component to use.

**Fix:**
1. Delete partial `unwrapPhase_bridging` dataset (crashed at pair 20/38):
```python
import h5py
with h5py.File('inputs/ifgramStack.h5', 'a') as f:
    if 'unwrapPhase_bridging' in f:
        del f['unwrapPhase_bridging']
```
2. In `smallbaselineApp.cfg`: `mintpy.unwrapError.method = no`
3. Re-run `correct_unwrap_error` (step effectively skips; pipeline advances to `invert_network`).

**Justification:** ALOS-1 L-band at 23.6 cm wavelength over this scene has minimal unwrapping errors. Urban coherence in the SW sector (Subic Bay/Olongapo) exceeded 0.7. Skipping bridging is acceptable.

**Automated in batch script v2.0:** Detects `CONNCOMP_EMPTY` pattern; deletes `unwrapPhase_bridging` dataset, sets `mintpy.unwrapError.method = no` in cfg, retries. Auto-heal error catalog entry: `CONNCOMP_EMPTY`.

---

### M3: `invert_network` — `IndexError: list index out of range` at `ifgram_inversion.py:732`

**Traceback signature:**
```
IndexError: list index out of range
  File ".../mintpy/ifgram_inversion.py", line 732
```

**Root cause:** `mintpy.load.waterMaskFile` and `mintpy.networkInversion.waterMaskFile` are **separate config keys** in MintPy 1.6.2. Setting `mintpy.load.waterMaskFile = no` (Fix M1) does NOT propagate to `invert_network`. The inversion key still pointed to `waterMask.rdr`; `ifgram_inversion.py` tried to open the all-zero binary ISCE2 raster as HDF5, found no `waterMask` dataset at any index, and crashed with `IndexError: list index out of range` at line 732.

**Fix:**
```bash
sed -i 's|mintpy.networkInversion.waterMaskFile.*|mintpy.networkInversion.waterMaskFile = no|' smallbaselineApp.cfg
```
Re-run `invert_network`.

**Rule for P447 (and likely P449):** Always set BOTH waterMask keys independently:
```ini
mintpy.load.waterMaskFile                = no   # waterMask.rdr is all-zero
mintpy.networkInversion.waterMaskFile    = no   # separate key — must set independently
```

**Automated in batch script v2.0:** Detects `INVERSION_WATERMASK` pattern; applies `sed` fix to cfg and retries. Auto-heal error catalog entry: `INVERSION_WATERMASK`.

---

**P447 F0300 final result:** 10,155 reliable pixels (tempCoh ≥ 0.7), 2.0% of 511,924 total. Coverage 15.503–16.139 N, 121.300–122.037 E (636 × 737 px geo, 0.001°). `velocity.h5` and `geo_velocity.kmz` confirmed written. All three errors (M1, M2, M3) are preemptively handled in `linog_batch_p447_mintpy.sh` v2.0 — F0310 processing should run without manual intervention.
